text:
jamie: quick follow-up from today's all-hands — thanks everyone. how should we succinctly position Redwood vs the big cloud vendors when platform teams ask? lead with perf/cost or deployment flexibility?

alex: great Q. start with the customer pain: unpredictable inference costs and ops burden. we then say: 1) predictable economics (dedicated + optimize), 2) unified runtime across hosted/dedicated/private, 3) production controls (rollouts/SLOs). perf and flexibility are the proof points. keep it short.

maria: +1 to alex. for sales pitches i recommend a 15s opener: “Redwood gives you consistent latency, lower per-token cost, and the option to deploy on-prem without rewriting your stack.” then show a single benchmark slide (latency & $/token).

sam: curious about the technical narrative — should eng-focused docs call out kernel/compiler differences vs cloud-managed stacks? or keep that under the hood?

lee: for eng audiences call out the runtime differentiators: continuous batching, KV cache, quant-friendly paths, and smart routing. keep it concrete — e.g., “50% lower tail latency on typical chat workloads vs naive hosters” (where we have the benchmark). for non-eng, omit kernels.

jamie: makes sense. how about competitor framing — do we name names (e.g., big cloud A, managed endpoint B) or talk in categories (cloud managed endpoints, open-hosters, self-hosted runtimes)?

alex: prefer categories in public collateral. in one-on-ones or RFPs call out specifics and show the cost/latency table. public claims need to be defensible.

taylor: from sales: customers ask whether Redwood is ‘just another endpoint’ or a replacement for their infra. recommended answer: "It’s a drop-in API for fast adoption, and a growth path to Dedicated/Private for predictable scale and compliance." keep the path explicit.

maria: roadmap tie-in — we should make the adoption path visible in product docs (e.g., banner: "Started on Hosted? Here's how to migrate to Dedicated in 3 steps"). I'll draft a short doc this sprint.

sam: follow-up re: metrics — can we standardize 3 easy benchmarks we expect to show (p50 latency, tail latency p99, and $/1M tokens)? ops-bot: link to current benchmark dashboard pls.

ops-bot: benchmark dashboard: https://redwood.internal/bench/2025-q4 (view restricted)

lee: also call out reliability examples — automatic fallbacks and multi-region routing. customers care about apps staying online more than shaving 10ms.

jamie: great call. last thing: competitive FAQs — can someone add a short FAQ snippet for the customer playbook? i can paste into slides.

maria: i'll add an FAQ draft in the product repo -> PR by EOD Friday. includes: "When do we recommend Dedicated vs Private?", "How do we measure cost savings?", and "What data residency controls exist?"

alex: thanks team. small comms ask: keep the external message consistent — i'll share a one-paragraph canonical pitch after i sync with gtm on Monday.

taylor: :thumbsup: will sync with AE leads and ask for competing objection examples.

jamie: thanks — that’ll do. recording + slides for folks who missed the all-hands:
ops-bot: recording: https://meetings.redwood/ah-2025-11-07 (automated post)

sam: also — will we have a short internal cheat sheet for engineers (one-pager) on when to recommend which deployment? could help PMs and SEs.

maria: yes, one-pager going into the product docs, cc jamie for slides.

lee: if anyone wants the raw perf numbers i used in the talk DM me and i’ll share the notebook (some work in progress).

jamie: awesome. wrapping up — thanks everyone, feel free to drop more Qs here or ping me.
